newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira weakness on EMU report unjustified - Fantozzi.
newsitem.headline: Lira weakness on EMU report unjustified - Fantozzi.

text.p: The lira's weakness this morning on reports of a plan to delay Italy's EMU entry was unjustified and Italy still aims to be in the first wave of members, Foreign Trade minister Augusto Fantozzi told Reuters.
The lira weakened to below its central ERM parity rate of 990 against the mark after a Financial Times report said Italy will be offered delayed entry to the single European currency.
At 1353 GMT the lira was quoted at 985.35/5.60 per mark.
"The lira's weakness this morning was unjustified even if there was certainly speculation involved. The Italian market is doing well and this means the trend is positive," he said.
Referring to the reported plan to allow Italy in EMU in 2000 or 2001, Fantozzi said, "everyone's playing their own game.
"There are political forces who have an interest in not having Italy in Europe. We must play our own game and that is exactly what the government is doing."
"I am convinced that Italy must be in (the first wave). Personally, and also for foreign trade reasons, I think we will be in," he said.
"A monetary Europe without Italy would be damaging for Europe," he said adding that as for the Maastricht parameters, "everyone's have difficulty with them, Germany included."
